newsitem.title: CHINA: China cuts contract tax on housing purchases.
newsitem.headline: China cuts contract tax on housing purchases.

text.p: China is to cut the contract tax paid on purchases of homes to 3.0 percent from 6.0 percent to boost consumption, officials said on Friday.

"This will happen very soon," an official of the Ministry of Construction said by telephone. "The State Council (the cabinet) has in principle agreed with the revised regulation on contract tax administration."
He said the tax paid by home buyers on purchase contracts would be cut to 3.0 percent from 6.0 percent, set in the 1950s. He gave no date for when the change would take effect.
The policy aimed to encourage people to buy houses, the China Securities newspaper said, quoting Hou Jie, Minister of Construction.
If housing sales could rise then a boom in construction could fuel economic growth, the newspaper quoted Hou as saying.
By the end of 1996, China had about 50 million square metres of vacant residential housing, occupying about 100 billion yuan ($12 billion) of capital.
